idiom_name: rebuild at exact size (lst = lst[:n], lst.copy()) or del lst[n:]
implementation_notes: A list has no capacity API, so the pattern is expressed through the operations CPython does expose: rebuild - lst[:n] or lst.copy() allocates a fresh array holding exactly the survivors, and the old array is dropped with the old object - or shrink in place by deleting a trailing slice (del lst[n:], lst[k:] = ...), which CPython services by reallocating once the new size falls far enough below the allocation (the interpreter's own comment: 'If the newsize falls lower than half the allocated size, then proceed with the realloc() to shrink the list'). bytearray and array.array have no trim method either, so trimming them means rebuilding (array.array(typecode, a[:n]), bytes(b[:n])) or deleting a trailing slice. Because rebinding replaces the object, every other reference - an attribute, closure, container slot or default argument - keeps the peak-sized list alive, which is exactly the leak the pattern is meant to fix.
code_sketch:
rows = [parse(line) for line in payload]     # peak ~250k rows
rows = [r for r in rows if r.keep]           # right-sized rebuild; old array dropped
# identity must survive:
# del rows[n:]      # or rows[n:] = []
#   CPython reallocates once the size falls below half the allocation
# bytearray / array.array: no trim - rebuild instead
pitfalls: Rebinding does not shrink the object other code still holds: a second reference (attribute, closure, container slot) keeps the peak-sized list alive, so the trim silently does nothing for the memory.
Deleting a trailing slice is documented as O(n - k) and does not promise to release anything (the halving reallocation is a CPython implementation detail); rebuilding always copies.

A live memoryview or other buffer export pins the storage and prevents resizing (BufferError: Existing exports of data), so drop the views before trimming - and remember a memoryview does not keep the trimmed list small either.
sources: docs.python.org, 5. Data Structures - list.copy() ('Return a shallow copy of the list. Similar to a[:]'), list.clear() ('Remove all items from the list. Similar to del a[:]') and the note that mutating list methods return None: https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/datastructures.html

CPython source, Objects/listobject.c (3.13) - list_resize: 'Bypass realloc() when a previous overallocation is large enough to accommodate the newsize. If the newsize falls lower than half the allocated size, then proceed with the realloc() to shrink the list', and list_slice_lock_held building slices with list_new_prealloc(len): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/3.13/Objects/listobject.c
